land.text: Lesbos, given to Francesco I Gattilusio as the dowry of John V's sister Maria Palaiologina

predecessors.note: Lesbos was an imperial island (infobox: Gattilusio under the Palaiologos); the lordship paid homage first to the emperor and from 1456 to the sultan.

land.text: Lesbos, 'captured by an Ottoman fleet in September 1462', ending the family's power

successors.note: Ainos had surrendered in January 1456 and the other islands went in 1456; Lemnos was held by a papal fleet in 1457 and by Venice in 1464 (Lemnos page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Lemnos acquired 'as a fief shortly before the Fall of Constantinople in 1453' (Lemnos page) and, undated, Imbros, Samothrace and the fortress of Kotsinos on Lemnos in the '15th century' (Gattilusi page). The Lemnos page: Mehmed II accepted Dorino's rule over Lemnos and Thasos for an annual tribute; after Dorino died in 1455 Domenico received only Lemnos.

New keyframe: after 1456 the Ottomans 'removed the Gattilusi from their remaining lands, except Lesbos', which they held for an annual payment of 4,000 gold pieces. (Reviewer eu-05-x, 2026-10-19: 'to' 1461 -> 1462: 'An Ottoman fleet captured the island in September 1462' (Gattilusi page), so Lesbos is drawn in 1462, the dissolve year)

ledger.note: 17 July 1355: John V Palaiologos makes Francesco Gattilusio lord of Lesbos. 'John V rewarded him with the title of Archon (Lord) of Lesbos' on 17 July 1355, the island offered 'as dowry for his sister' Maria, for his help in retaking Constantinople from John VI Kantakouzenos in December 1354. The Gattilusi page has the marriage and the reward in 1355.

region.text: Ainos (Enez) and its salt pans, on the Thracian coast

ledger.note: About 1384: the Gattilusi hold Ainos (Enez). 'From ca. 1384 on the city came under the rule of the Genoese Gattilusio family'; it paid 'an annual tribute to the Ottomans' and lived on salt pans and fisheries. The Gattilusi page's infobox gives Niccolo as lord of Ainos from 1376 or 1382; the page names no granter, so Byzantium is the researcher's reading.

1440s: Thasos joins the lordship. Bridging: the infobox fragments of the Gattilusi page give 'Thasos (1440s)' and the 15th-century acquisitions list Thasos with no year; the decade's first year is used. Previous holder unnamed (Byzantine nominal overlord assumed).

region.text: Lemnos 'as a fief shortly before the Fall of Constantinople in 1453'; Imbros and Samothrace in the 15th century

ledger.note: About 1453: Dorino I Gattilusio receives Lemnos as a fief 'shortly before the Fall of Constantinople in 1453'. Imbros and Samothrace appear in the Gattilusi page's list of 15th-century acquisitions with no year, so they are placed here at confidence 1; the year for Lemnos is the page's.

region.text: the Gattilusi's remaining lands except Lesbos

ledger.note: 1456: the Ottomans take the north Aegean islands. The Ottomans 'removed the Gattilusi from their remaining lands, except Lesbos' and appointed Michael Critobulus governor of Imbros; the Lemnos page has Mehmed capture 'the Gattilusi domains in Thrace' in 1456 and Lemnos's Greeks submit to the sultan (Hamza Bey as governor). The page gives no island-by-island dates.

region.text: Ainos (Enez) and its salt pans, on the Thracian coast

ledger.note: January 1456: Ainos surrenders to Mehmed II. The city was forced to 'surrender in January 1456' after Helena Notaras appealed to the sultan in a dispute with Dorino II; Mehmed attacked by land and sea.
September 1462: the Ottoman fleet takes Lesbos. 'an Ottoman fleet captured the island in September 1462', ending the family's power; Niccolo was sent to Constantinople as a prisoner.
September 1462: the Gattilusi lordship ends after 107 years. Infobox 'End of rule: Ottoman conquest of Lesbos, 1462'.

wars.outcome: An Ottoman fleet captured Lesbos in September 1462; Niccolo Gattilusio was taken to Constantinople.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row; slug free ('gattilusi' follows the Wikipedia title). Four pages opened. Not settled: (1) Thasos, Imbros and Samothrace have no year on any page opened (ledger 1440 and 1453 entries are confidence 1 for them); (2) Ainos 1376 (Gattilusi infobox), 1382 or ca. 1384 (Enez page); (3) the Old Phokaia lordship (c.1416-1426/8, infobox) and the Gattilusi of Ainos as a separate line (Niccolo 1376-1409, Palamede 1409-1455, Dorino II 1455-56) are not drawn separately; (4) the succession tables on the Gattilusi page are partly garbled (rulers carry a note); (5) the annual tribute to the Ottomans (4,000 gold pieces for Lesbos from 1456; for Lemnos and Thasos under Dorino; from Ainos) is not territorial and belongs in the Ottoman dossier as vassal events (counterpart 'gattilusi'). Lemnos was Venetian 1464-1479. Island coordinates used because Lemnos, Thasos, Imbros, Samothrace and Enez are not in the gazetteer.
